ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, one end of a light straight rod of length L can rotate about the fixed axis O, and the other end is fixed to a small ball of mass m. The small ball rests on a horizontal lifting platform, and the lifting platform rises uniformly at speed v. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: When the angle between the rod and the vertical direction is α, the angular velocity of the rod is $\frac{v}{L\sin\alpha}$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, one end of a light straight rod of length L can rotate about the fixed axis O, and the other end is fixed to a small ball of mass m. The small ball rests on a horizontal lifting platform, and the lifting platform rises uniformly at speed v. When the angle between the rod and the vertical direction is α, what is the angular velocity of the rod?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When the angle between the rod and the vertical direction is α, the angular velocity of the rod is $\frac{v}{L\sin\alpha}$
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the upper part of the figure there is a fixed support, and one end of the light rod is hinged at the fixed axis O; a vertical dashed line is drawn downward from O as the vertical reference direction. The light rod slants toward the lower left, and the other end is connected to a black small ball. The small ball is just resting on the upper surface of the horizontal lifting platform. On the right side of the lifting platform there is an upward arrow, labeled with speed v, indicating that the platform rises uniformly. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take O as the origin and the vertically downward direction as the positive direction. The rod length is L, and the angle between the rod and the vertical direction is α, so the vertical coordinate of the small ball relative to O is y = L cos α. Since the small ball rests on the horizontal lifting platform and moves upward together with the platform at speed v, while the positive coordinate direction is taken as vertically downward, the rate of change of the small ball's vertical coordinate is dy/dt = -v. Differentiate y = L cos α with respect to time to obtain dy/dt = -L sin α · dα/dt. Let the angular velocity ω = dα/dt, then -L sin α · ω = -v, solving gives ω = v/(L sin α).
